title: Bram and the Bakery
premise: Edmund Ishikawa built her wedding-planning empire on the ruins of her own abandoned engagement, hiding behind flawless events she refuses to feel. When a letter she wrote eleven years ago—never sent, postmarked the week she vanished from Bram Okafor's life—surfaces in his late grandmother's bakery, Edmund is forced back to the small coastal town where she once belonged. As she plans the festival that could save Bram's struggling bakery and her own reputation, old truths about why she left unravel: she fled to protect him from her family's collapse, not because she stopped loving him. At the festival's climax, with a career-defining contract in one hand and Bram's flour-dusted hand in the other, Edmund finally chooses to be seen—and they rebuild the bakery, and each other, together.
about_author: Tamsin Halloran is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, coastal towns, and the spaces between what we say and what we mean. She lives in Oregon with her partner and an opinionated sourdough starter named Duchess.

chapters.title: The Letter That Waited
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. While cataloguing the estate of Bram's late grandmother for a client, Edmund finds an unsent letter addressed to Bram—in her own handwriting, postmarked eleven years ago. Panic and longing collide as she pockets it instead of delivering it. Emotional beat: denial dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Sugar and Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram, running his grandmother's failing bakery, learns the festival committee hired a famous planner: Edmund Ishikawa. He hasn't said her name aloud in years. He decides to treat her like any vendor. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Their first meeting is all clipboards and cold politeness, but the bakery smells like every summer she lost. She overcommits to the festival to prove she feels nothing. Emotional beat: control as armor.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sorting his grandmother's things, Bram finds a tin of Edmund's favorite recipe cards, annotated in her hand. His sister Priya pushes him to ask Edmund why she left; he refuses. Emotional beat: loyalty to a wound.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Perfect Events
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the city, Edmund lands a career-making offer: plan a celebrity wedding that would make her firm untouchable—but it conflicts with festival dates. Her business partner warns her not to go back at all. Emotional beat: ambition as escape route.

chapters.title: Flour Fight
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A delivery disaster forces Edmund to work a shift in the bakery. Banter turns into laughter, then a near-kiss interrupted by Priya. Bram pretends it meant nothing. Emotional beat: warmth breaking through frost.

chapters.title: The Version of Me You Knew
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund drafts a confession about the letter, then burns the draft. A flashback reveals her family's bankruptcy the week of their engagement—the reason she disappeared. Emotional beat: shame recast as selflessness.

chapters.title: Festival Politics
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The town council threatens to relocate the festival to a rival venue; a developer circles the bakery block. Bram realizes Edmund's event might be the bakery's last chance—or its public funeral. Emotional beat: stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Rain on the Promenade
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Storm cancels a site walkthrough; stranded under an awning, Edmund and Bram finally argue about why she left. She lies by omission. He sees it. Emotional beat: truth deferred, intimacy deepening anyway.

chapters.title: Priya's Question
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Priya confronts Edmund directly: 'Did you ever read his replies?' Edmund learns Bram wrote to her for two years after she left—letters her mother intercepted. Emotional beat: the ground shifting.

chapters.title: The Celebrity Wedding
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the city, Edmund watches a bride cry over a cake and feels nothing but exhaustion. She declines the career-defining contract, stunning her partner. Emotional beat: the first honest choice.

chapters.title: Recipe Cards
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram bakes his grandmother's cardamom buns from Edmund's annotated cards and admits to himself he never stopped waiting. He resolves to ask her one straight question at the festival rehearsal. Emotional beat: hope re-armed.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Festival rehearsal goes beautifully until the developer announces a buyout bid timed to fail the festival. Edmund publicly vows the show will go on—binding herself to the town she once fled. Emotional beat: commitment before courage.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Priya finds proof among their grandmother's papers that Edmund's mother returned Bram's letters unopened. Bram's anger curdles into something worse: understanding. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Cornered by guilt, Edmund finally reads her own eleven-year-old letter aloud alone in the empty bakery: it was a goodbye she never had the right to send. She decides to tell Bram everything tomorrow. Emotional beat: reckoning.

chapters.title: Everything, Then
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Edmund confesses—the bankruptcy, the intercepted letters, the unsent goodbye. Bram walks out mid-sentence. The festival opens in forty-eight hours without its planner's heart. Emotional beat: rupture.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Running on no sleep, Edmund salvages collapsing vendors, a broken stage, and a sponsor pullout while the town watches whether she'll quit like she did before. Emotional beat: endurance as apology.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The developer offers Bram enough money to erase his debts—if he pulls the bakery out of the festival and lets it fail publicly. Holding the pen, he thinks of his grandmother's tin. Emotional beat: temptation at its peak.

chapters.title: Opening Night
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The festival opens in chaos and glory; Bram arrives at the last minute with trays of cardamom buns and signs nothing. Across the crowd they see each other clearly for the first time. Emotional beat: arrival.

chapters.title: Read It Aloud
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On the darkened promenade after closing, Bram asks Edmund to read the letter—to him, this time. She does, voice breaking, and adds the ending she never wrote: I choose you, out loud, in front of everyone. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Second Proofing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Weeks later: the bakery survives, renamed with both their names on the lease. Edmund dissolves her city firm and starts a small studio planning only celebrations she believes in. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt.

chapters.title: Bram and the Bakery
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. One year later, at the second annual festival, Bram proposes with a ring baked inside a cardamom bun—terrible idea, perfect them. Edmund says yes before he finishes asking. Emotional beat: joy earned twice.
